ruling.verbatim:
Yes. This result changes the priority of the project.
The key finding is not merely that centroids/prototypes failed. It is that on text, the partition abstraction itself is spending the retrieval budget badly. MuSiQue goes from 0.660 with 50 blocks to 0.882 with a matched-size flat list, and even the frozen composite is only 0.760; SQuAD shows the same direction. MetaQA reverses dramatically: partitions get ~0.64–0.80 while flat is only ~0.39.
And the budget curve makes this much harder to dismiss as just bad block ranking: on MuSiQue, flat reaches ~0.66 ALL-gold with only ~500 nodes, while the partition route needs ~5,100 nodes to reach ~0.66. On SQuAD, flat top-100 is already ~0.99. MetaQA is exactly the opposite.
So I would make a narrow reopening of the L1 freeze.
Not “reopen L1 and start trying ideas again.” Only one falsifiable question:
Are partitions actually necessary, or is the KB gain just graph expansion/co-location?\boxed{ \text{Are partitions actually necessary, or is the KB gain just graph expansion/co-location?} }
Your own report already identifies this confound correctly: MetaQA's partition system gets STRUCT-aware blocks, structural vote propagation, and the H2 beam, whereas the flat comparator is text-only. Therefore the present experiment does not isolate the contribution of partitioning.
The next experiment I would preregister
Call it something like:
FLAT_BALANCED_H2\texttt{FLAT\_BALANCED\_H2}
with no partitions anywhere.
Start from the frozen Dense + SPLADE flat node ranking. Then reserve exactly one block-equivalent of the total context for the same frozen BALANCED_H2 graph expansion already used by the composite.
For a total budget MM and patch capacity C≈100C\approx100:
context=top (M−C) flat semantic nodes⏟semantic base+up to C novel BALANCED-H2 nodes⏟graph patch.\text{context} = \underbrace{\text{top }(M-C)\text{ flat semantic nodes}}_{\text{semantic base}} + \underbrace{\text{up to }C\text{ novel BALANCED-H2 nodes}}_{\text{graph patch}}.
If H2 produces fewer than CC novel nodes, fill the remainder using the next flat-ranked nodes.
So conceptually:

```text
QUERY
 │
 ├── Dense
 │
 └── SPLADE
       │
   flat node RRF
       │
 top M−C nodes
       │
       ├───────────────┐
       │               │
       │        same frozen seeds
       │               │
       │       real STRUCT edges
       │               │
       │       BALANCED H2 beam
       │               │
       └────── + C novel nodes
                    │
               exactly M nodes
```

No PHG.
No H4_SK.
No block ownership.
No node→block voting.
No SAFE.
No QMAX block aggregation.
And critically, no new scoring mechanism.
That makes it a clean ablation of the thing we actually care about.
Why this is the decisive comparison
Suppose MetaQA does:
flat=0.39\text{flat}=0.39flat+H2≈0.78\text{flat+H2}\approx0.78partition+H2≈0.80.\text{partition+H2}\approx0.80.
Then most of what we have been attributing to partitions was actually:
semantic seeds + real graph traversal\boxed{\text{semantic seeds + real graph traversal}}
and we should seriously consider deleting partitioning from the universal retrieval architecture.
On the other hand, suppose:
flat+H2=0.60\text{flat+H2}=0.60
while
partition+H2=0.80.\text{partition+H2}=0.80.
Then partitions are doing something genuinely important: co-locating related answer sets so one retrieval unit exposes many graph-connected answers efficiently.
Either result is scientifically valuable.
This also resolves your IVF question
I would stop pursuing centroid/prototype routing for now.
Your §28 result already says fixed representatives do not solve the problem: up to 32 representatives per block still lose on text, and only scoring all nodes recovers node-voting-like behavior.
That tells us something deeper:
the issue isn't “we need a better approximation of node voting.”
It may be:
on text datasets we shouldn't route through blocks at all.
That's much more important.
QMAX itself supports this interpretation. Even if you perform the strongest possible semantic block score,
S(B,q)=max⁡v∈Bq⊤ev,S(B,q)=\max_{v\in B}q^\top e_v,
MuSiQue still reaches only about 0.70, whereas flat Dense alone reaches about 0.87. So the relevant node is being found; the damage happens when we pay for its entire block.
That's granularity waste, not routing failure.
Which is interesting because PATCH1 already taught us the same lesson from the other direction:
when H2 finds useful nodes spread over many blocks, packing the nodes directly is vastly better than buying all their owner blocks.
Now flat-vs-partition says the same phenomenon may apply to the entire text retrieval stage.
Where I would validate it
I agree completely that DEV_A is finished for mechanism selection, and DEV_B should not become DEV_C-by-repetition. Your report explicitly records that constraint.
The nice consequence of removing partitions is that the infrastructure blockage becomes much less important.
2Wiki and HotpotQA are suddenly especially attractive. Their missing PHG partitions no longer matter. If their frozen node embeddings, Dense/SPLADE retrieval and STRUCT adjacency already exist, then we can test `FLAT_BALANCED_H2` without building PHG at all.
I would preregister:

* HotpotQA split A: untouched text transfer.
* 2Wiki split A: untouched multi-hop text transfer.
* WebQSP train_holdout: untouched KB transfer, if the existing RoG STRUCT graph and node retrieval assets are enough to execute the beam without PHG.

That gives us precisely what we need:

```text
Hotpot / 2Wiki
    Does flat + graph preserve the enormous flat advantage on text?

WebQSP
    Does graph expansion rescue NAME_ONLY flat retrieval on a KB
    without graph partitions?
```

And WebQSP becomes particularly valuable because the damned PHG resource contention no longer blocks this question.
I would freeze the hypothesis before any run
My ruling would be:
Reopen the frozen L1 design for one isolated architectural ablation only: `FLAT_BALANCED_H2`, testing whether fixed graph partitions are necessary once flat semantic retrieval receives the same bounded real-edge expansion privilege. No other mechanism classes are reopened. DEV_A and DEV_B remain unavailable for selection.
Primary comparison on fresh populations:
FLATvsFLAT_BALANCED_H2\texttt{FLAT} \quad\text{vs}\quad \texttt{FLAT\_BALANCED\_H2}
with a fixed total node budget.
Where a canonical partition result eventually exists, also compare against:
QMAX_BALANCED_H2_PATCH1.\texttt{QMAX\_BALANCED\_H2\_PATCH1}.
But partition availability should no longer be required to run the new hypothesis.
And there is a genuinely attractive possible endpoint here.
We may end up with something much simpler than the current architecture:
flat semantic retrieval→bounded graph expansion→direct node-level context\boxed{ \text{flat semantic retrieval} \rightarrow \text{bounded graph expansion} \rightarrow \text{direct node-level context} }
instead of:
semantic retrieval→node voting→partitions→SAFE→graph beam→virtual patch.\text{semantic retrieval} \rightarrow \text{node voting} \rightarrow \text{partitions} \rightarrow \text{SAFE} \rightarrow \text{graph beam} \rightarrow \text{virtual patch}.
If the simple version transfers, that is not a disappointing result. It would be a stronger paper result because we experimentally discovered that coarse graph partitioning was unnecessary once the right node-level semantic + structural composition was used.
And if it fails on WebQSP while remaining superior on text, then we have isolated something equally useful: hard graph regions are beneficial specifically when semantic node identity is insufficient and answers are structurally related but semantically opaque.
That is now the experiment I would run before spending another minute optimizing partition centroids.

question: Are partitions actually necessary, or is the KB gain just graph expansion/co-location?

design.FLAT_RRF: the frozen Dense + SPLADE node RRF extended to full depth (section 29): exhaustive fp32 dense products (unit queries x fp16->fp32 node rows) and fp32 SPLADE products; fv = 1/(K0 + p_dense) + 1/(K0 + p_splade), 0-based positions over all N nodes, float64; a node without a positive SPLADE score takes the SPLADE list depth; descending, ties -> dense order
design.FLAT_BALANCED_H2@M: FLAT_RRF[:M - C] (semantic base) + the first C nodes of the frozen BALANCED_H2 beam (bal1 then bal2, first-visit order) that are not in the base (graph patch) + FLAT_RRF[M - C:] minus the patch, in order, until exactly M nodes (fill)
design.C: 100 = one block-equivalent (npart = N // 100 blocks of mean size 100; cap = round(N / npart) = 100 on every corpus)
design.BALANCED_H2: the frozen section-21 beam of the composite, unchanged: seeds = node_rrf(served dense top-200, served SPLADE top-200)[:5] (the replay-cache rule), depth 2 over the directed STRUCT family, out-edges always and in-edges only at a non-hub (deg_u + 1 > cap), dst / dir / mid transition geometry fused by RRF (K0 = 60), per-parent round-robin compression to BEAM = 100 per hop; the function source text of _l1c_microl3.py and _l1c_transfer_composite.py is exec'd verbatim (sha256 per function below)
design.no_partition_anywhere: no PHG, no H4_SK, no block ownership, no node->block voting, no SAFE, no QMAX block aggregation, no new scoring mechanism
design.gold_metric: ALL-gold coverage (every gold node of the query inside the served context) is primary; ANY is descriptive

comparisons.D1 (PRIMARY, fresh, one-shot): per fresh dataset, split A: FLAT@5000 (reference) vs FLAT_BALANCED_H2@5000 (arm); exact two-sided McNemar on the ALL-gold indicators; GAIN if gained > lost and p < 0.01, LOSS if lost > gained and p < 0.01, else NEUTRAL
comparisons.D2 (DEV_A, non-selecting): PRIMARY = QMAX_BALANCED_H2_PATCH1 (its per-row ALL indicator from the section-29 record) vs FLAT_BALANCED_H2 at PRIMARY's per-query exposure B_q; same test and labels
comparisons.D3 (DEV_A, non-selecting): FLAT@B_q vs FLAT_BALANCED_H2@B_q; same test and labels
comparisons.descriptive: fixed M in (500, 1000, 2000, 5000); strata by hop and by gold count; patch statistics (novel nodes, hop-1 share, fill); gold accounting (rescued by the patch, displaced from the FLAT tail); ANY

FRESH_VERDICT.FLAT_BALANCED_H2_UNIVERSAL: no fresh D1 = LOSS and webqsp D1 = GAIN
FRESH_VERDICT.NO_KB_GAIN: no fresh D1 = LOSS and webqsp D1 != GAIN

DEV_A_KB_READING (diagnostic).PARTITIONS_BEAT_FLAT_H2_ON_THE_DEV_A_KB: metaqa and metaqa_phg D2 both LOSS
DEV_A_KB_READING (diagnostic).PARTITIONS_NOT_SHOWN_NECESSARY_ON_THE_DE: metaqa and metaqa_phg D2 both NEUTRAL or GAIN
